plugin.name: xRewind
plugin.description: Every change, logged. Any of it, undone.

subcommands.description: Where the history is kept, what's saved and waiting, and any problem.
Reloads config.yml and the language files, and applies them.

permissions.description: Turn the inspector on and off with /xrewind inspect.
Search the history: /xrewind lookup, page and near.
See chat and commands in lookups (a:chat, a:command), which are more private than blocks.
Roll back, preview, apply, cancel and undo: /xrewind rollback, apply, cancel and undo.
Roll back past rollback.max-radius, or a whole world (r:#world) or every world (r:#global).
Put back what a rollback undid: /xrewind restore.
See whether logging is keeping up, with /xrewind status.
Every admin subcommand of xRewind, and its update notices.
Hear about newer versions of xRewind when joining.

header: xRewind: every change, logged. Any of it, undone.
Apply changes with /xrewind reload (or /xr reload): everything applies, what's logged and
where it's stored included. A bad value falls back to its default with a warning in the
console; xRewind never stops over config. The messages are in lang/.

comment: How this plugin's messages look, and the language they're in. shared uses the
setting in plugins/Xena/config.yml, which every Xena plugin reads; anything else is
this plugin's own.
The language players see messages in: auto for each player's own (their client's
language setting), or one language for everyone, such as de or pt-BR.
The language of the console, and of players whose language has no file in lang/.
The look every message shares, used in messages as tags: <prefix>, <highlight>,
<success> and <error>. Colours are names (gray, gold) or hex (#B48CFF), with bold,
italic, underlined, strikethrough or obfuscated if you like: <#B48CFF><bold>.
<prefix> starts the default messages. Make it your server's name, such as
"<dark_gray>[<gradient:#B48CFF:#5EE08A>MyServer</gradient>]</dark_gray> ", or blank for none.
The colour of message text that has no tag of its own.
<highlight>: names and values, such as a player or a speed.
<success>: something turned on or done.
<error>: something refused or turned off.
Where this plugin keeps its data. Read at startup only: restart after changing it.
sqlite keeps everything in one file in the plugin's folder, with nothing to set up.
mysql (or MariaDB) is for networks, or servers with a lot of history.
shared keeps it in the database every Xena plugin can share, set in plugins/Xena/config.yml.
Put in front of every table's name, so plugins and servers can share one database.
Only for type: mysql.
Extra connection settings, as in a JDBC URL: useSSL=true&serverTimezone=UTC.
The connections used to read, beside the one that writes.
How many: 0 picks for the database (1 for SQLite, 2 for MySQL). More helps only a
MySQL server that many reads wait on.
What's logged. Something that's off isn't even listened for, so it costs nothing.
Changes apply on /xrewind reload.
Blocks players break, with what they held, and blocks that fall off with them.
Blocks players place, and what they replaced.
Blocks explosions destroy. TNT is put down to whoever lit it.
Blocks burnt away, and fires players light.
Buckets, and flowing water or lava destroying a block. Plain spreading isn't logged.
Blocks pistons move.
Endermen, withers, ravagers, falling sand. Sheep eating grass and villagers farming aren't.
Text written on signs. Bukkit only: Fabric has no event for it.
Items players put into or take out of containers.
Items hoppers and droppers move. Busy on farms.
Mobs and players killed by players.
Doors, trapdoors, gates, levers and buttons players use.
Leaves decaying.
Players joining and quitting, and where.
Chat messages. Off by default for players' privacy; lookups need xrewind.lookup.chat.
Commands players run. Off by default; lookups need xrewind.lookup.chat. Bukkit only:
Fabric has no event before a command runs.
Worlds nothing is logged in, by name: world_nether on Bukkit, minecraft:the_nether on Fabric.
Rollbacks and restores. Blocks are set a few milliseconds per tick, chunk by chunk (each
region on its own thread on Folia), so even a big one doesn't freeze the server, and
without physics, so nothing cascades. One stopped by a restart carries on when the
server starts again.
How long a rollback may work each tick, in milliseconds. A tick is 50.
The radius, in blocks, when a rollback doesn't give one with r:.
The largest r: without the xrewind.rollback.global permission, which r:#world and
r:#global also need.
Deleting old history, so the database doesn't grow forever.
Delete history older than this many days, once a day. 0 keeps everything. A
rollback can't reach further back than what's kept.
Telling you when a newer version is out: in the console, and to players with
<plugin>.admin.update when they join. Asks Modrinth once a day, off the server's threads,
sending only the plugin's version, the platform and the Minecraft version.
Whether to ask at all.
Which releases to hear of: release, beta (betas and releases) or alpha (everything).
Under a long list in chat (/homes, /history, ...) when it has more than one page.
<previous> and <next> are the list's command for those pages; what's inside
<has_previous>...</has_previous> or <has_next>...</has_next> shows only when there's such a page.
In the console, and to players with <plugin>.admin.update as they join, when a newer version is out
on the update channel the config picks. <url> is its download page.
/<plugin> debug, before the health checks' results.
/<plugin> debug: the database answered. <database> is where it is, such as "MySQL at db:3306/minecraft".
/<plugin> debug: the database didn't answer. <reason> is the driver's, in English.
/<plugin> debug: every plugin or mod it depends on is there. <names> lists them, or says none.

messages.english: <gold>!</gold> Dependencies: <names> not installed, so what needs them is off.
comment: /<plugin> debug: optional plugins or mods that aren't installed.
/<plugin> debug: plugins or mods it needs that aren't installed.

messages.english: <success>✔</success> Threads: tasks run where they should (<threading>).
comment: /<plugin> debug: a task on the global thread and one off it each ran where it should.
<threading> is how the server runs work, in English: "Folia's regions", "one main thread".
/<plugin> debug: a task ran on the wrong thread, or didn't run. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> debug: the config and language files had nothing wrong when they were last read.
/<plugin> debug: problems found the last time the files were read; the console and the report have them all.
/<plugin> debug: every module the config turns on is running.
/<plugin> debug: modules that failed. The report says why.
/<plugin> debug: a check that didn't finish. <check> is its name and <reason> why, in English.

messages.english: <prefix>Debug report: <click:open_url:'<url>'><hover:show_text:'Open it'><highlight><url></highlight></hover></click>. Share this link when asking for help; passwords and tokens are removed.
comment: /<plugin> debug: the report's link at a paste service (mclo.gs).

messages.english: <prefix>Couldn't upload the debug report (<reason>), so it's in <highlight><file></highlight> in the plugin's folder.
comment: /<plugin> debug: the upload failed, so the report was written to a file. <reason> is in English.

messages.english: <prefix>Debug report saved as <highlight><file></highlight> in the plugin's folder.
comment: /<plugin> debug, when uploading is turned off.
/<plugin> debug: the report couldn't be uploaded or written. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> import: the other plugin's files or tables weren't found.

messages.english: <prefix><error>An import is already running; wait for it to finish.</error>
comment: /<plugin> import while one is running.

messages.english: <prefix>Dry run from <source>: <highlight><importable></highlight> of <total> records would be imported, <skipped> skipped. Nothing was changed.
comment: /<plugin> import <source> --dry-run: what a real run would do.
/<plugin> import: the run starts.

messages.english: <prefix>Carrying on the import from <source> where it stopped, after <done> of <total> records...
comment: /<plugin> import: a run that stopped before is carried on.
/<plugin> import: progress, every few seconds.
/<plugin> import: one record that failed. The import carries on; the console lists them all.
/<plugin> import: the run finished.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The import from <source> stopped: <reason></error> Run it again to carry on where it left off.
comment: /<plugin> import: the run stopped, such as when the other plugin's database went away. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> migrate to the storage type in use.

messages.english: <prefix><error>A migration is already running; wait for it to finish.</error>
comment: /<plugin> migrate while one is running.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The <type> database already has data (<tables>).</error> Add --force to replace it with this server's.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: the target isn't empty. <tables> lists its tables with their rows.
/<plugin> migrate: the copy starts.
/<plugin> migrate: one table is copied.

messages.english: <prefix><success>Moved the data to <type> and checked it (rows: <rows>).</success> The plugin now uses <type>.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: done; the config's storage type was changed and applied.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Moving the data to <type> failed: <reason></error> The plugin still uses <from>.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: it failed, and the storage type wasn't changed. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> forget: the name isn't one the server knows. A UUID works too.
/<plugin> forget: done.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Some of <player>'s data couldn't be deleted (<failed>).</error> Records deleted: <records>. Run it again.
comment: /<plugin> forget: part of it failed. <failed> lists what, with why, in English.
/<plugin> reload: config.yml and the language files were read again and applied.
What's inside <has_one>...</has_one> shows when one module is on, <has_many>...</has_many> otherwise.
/<plugin> reload: one line per problem found in the files, in English. The console has them too.
/<plugin> reload: a module that failed, and why, in English.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Reloading <plugin> failed; the console has the details.
comment: /<plugin> reload: something went wrong; the settings from before are still in use.
Rare: a command that went away as it was typed.

messages.english: <prefix><error>You don't have permission to do that.
comment: The sender lacks the command's permission.
The console or a command block ran a command only players can use.
The command was typed with missing or extra words. <usage> is how to type it.
No player the sender can see is online by the name typed (<player>).
A number was expected. <input> is what was typed.
A whole number was expected. <input> is what was typed.
A number below the least the command takes (<min>).
A number above the most the command takes (<max>).
A word that isn't one of those the command takes (<choices>, comma-separated).
What was typed can't be used: true or false, a length of time, a name. <reason> is in English.
The command has a cooldown. <time> is how long is left.
A command that needs confirming, such as forget. <line> is the command, <time> how long there is.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Something went wrong running that command; the console has the details.
comment: The command hit an error. The console has what happened.

messages.english: <prefix>xRewind <highlight><version></highlight> on <platform>: <storage>. <gray>/xrewind lookup | rollback | restore | status | reload | debug
comment: /xrewind on its own, and /xrewind info.
Above a page of results. <count> is how many there are in all.
Above the history of one block, from the inspector.
One change. <ago> is how long ago, <user> who, <action> what they did, <block> what
to (a block, items, a mob, or what they wrote), <x> <y> <z> <world> where.
A change that's been rolled back.
Below a page. <page>, <pages>, and <next>: the command for the next page.
Nothing matched.
Sent while waiting on the database.
The parameters were wrong. <reason> says how (params.*).

messages.english: <prefix><error>Look something up first, then use /xrewind page.
comment: There's no previous lookup for /xrewind page.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The database isn't ready yet. /xrewind status says why.
comment: The database isn't ready yet.

messages.english: <prefix>Inspector <success>on</success>. Click a block to see its history; place one to see what was there.

comment: The words for each kind of change, as <action> shows them.
1.x had these in English only.

messages.english: <arg> isn't a parameter. Use u:, t:, r:, a:, i:, e: or w:, such as t:1h.
<key>: isn't a parameter. Use u:, t:, r:, a:, i:, e: or w:.
r:<value> isn't a radius. Use a number of blocks, #world or #global.
a:<value> isn't an action. Use block, +block, -block, container, +container, -container, kill, click, sign, chat, command or session.
<value> isn't a block or an item.
t:<value> isn't a time. Use a number and a unit, such as 30m, 6h, 2d or 1w.
From the console, add w:\<world> or r:#global.
From the console, use r:#world with w:\<world>, or r:#global.
<prefix><error>Add a time, such as <highlight>t:1h</highlight>, so it can't reach further back than you meant.
comment: A rollback or restore without t:.

messages.english: <prefix><error>That's past the <highlight><max></highlight>-block limit. r:#world, r:#global and bigger radii need <highlight>xrewind.rollback.global</highlight>.
comment: Past max-radius without permission. <max> is the limit.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Another rollback is running. Wait for it to finish.
comment: Another one is already running.

messages.english: <prefix>Previewing <highlight><count></highlight> blocks, for you only. <click:run_command:'/xrewind apply'><hover:show_text:'/xrewind apply'><success>[Apply]</success></hover></click> <click:run_command:'/xrewind cancel'><hover:show_text:'/xrewind cancel'><error>[Cancel]</error></hover></click>
comment: A #preview is showing. <count> is how many blocks.

messages.english: <prefix><error>You have no preview. Add #preview to a rollback or restore.

comment: On the action bar while it works.
When it's finished.

messages.english: <prefix><error><count> blocks were stored by a Minecraft version this one can't read, and were left as they are.
comment: Stored blocks this server couldn't read.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Nothing to undo. Undo works on your last rollback or restore since the server started.
<prefix><error>Another plugin stopped it before it started. Nothing changed.
comment: Another plugin stopped a rollback, restore or undo before it started.
<verb> in rollback.progress and rollback.done.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Purge history at least a day old: <highlight>t:1d</highlight> or more.
comment: A purge of less than a day.
<count> changes deleted; <time> how old.

messages.english: <prefix>Importing CoreProtect's history from <highlight><source></highlight>. Logging carries on meanwhile; the console shows progress.
comment: <source> is where CoreProtect's history is read from.

messages.english: <prefix><error>CoreProtect's history was already imported (<date>). <highlight>#again</highlight> imports it again, and what came across before shows twice.
comment: It was imported before.
CoreProtect's database couldn't be read.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The purge was stopped partway, after deleting <highlight><count></highlight> changes. Run it again to finish.
comment: The server stopped a purge partway.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The import was stopped partway. Run it again with <highlight>#again</highlight>; what came across before shows twice.
<prefix><error>CoreProtect is a Bukkit plugin, so there's nothing of it to import on this server.
comment: /xrewind import on Fabric.

messages.english:
<prefix><highlight>Storage</highlight>: <storage>
<highlight>Saved</highlight> since startup: <written> changes. Waiting: <waiting>. Missed: <missed>.
<highlight>Last batch</highlight>: <batch>
<highlight>Problem</highlight>: <problem>
comment: Whether logging is keeping up. <batch> is status.batch or status.no-batch, <problem> what's stopping writes or status.no-problem.

events.description: Someone looked the history up: a command, the inspector or a plugin. For an audit log; not cancellable.
A rollback, restore or undo is about to start. Cancel it to stop it.
A rollback, restore or undo finished, with what it did and its undo.
